title: [CQ-V09] Consumer policy dependency readiness
description:

Deliverable: Consumer policy dependency readiness. This is task V09 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

implementationPlan.description:
FIXTURE REALISM, the only edit to an existing test. In packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.strong.test.ts, `setDone` (line 249) today flips task-1 to DONE with a direct state write, so no qa_approve record exists.

Three CQ-V04 rows then assert that a bare consumer `unmetDependsOn(h.state, { dependsOn: ['task-1'] })` sees task-1 as delivered under live verified-local: V2 (:274), UC3 (:367) and UC6 (:405). Under V09 that consumer is strict, and a DONE without an approval is exactly the 'DONE by status alone' that must not count. Those three rows would fail.

Make setDone also store qa_approve's record, an approving Review on the current candidate:
```
h.state.reviews.set(`review-${cand}`, { id: `review-${cand}`, taskId: 'task-1', candidateId: cand, reviewerId: 'qa-1', decision: 'approve', summary: 'verified', createdAt: '2026-10-30T00:00:00.000Z' })
```
Give it a one-line comment citing CQ-V09.

NO expectation changes. The six setDone callers keep their asserted values; rows expecting ['task-1'] stay unmet on their other tokens. The architect ran it: with this +7 line edit and the step-3 predicate, the file passes 83/83 and the whole suite equals baseline. It also passes against today's predicate, which ignores reviews, so do this before step 3 and the suite never goes red.

implementationPlan.description:
DIRECT CALLERS AND REMOVAL AUDIT.

(a) tools/claimNextTask.ts dependsOnClaimRefusal (:252). Compute `dependencyShortfall(state, id, task)` with the claimed task as the consumer. Only an unmet prerequisite whose status is DONE may take the DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING branch, so its 'is DONE but lacks' text stays true. A strict consumer's missing, ARCHIVED-without-proof or unfinished prerequisites go to the status refusal, each rendered with describeUnmetDependency(state, id, task) so its tokens and the set_task_dependencies remedy show. A legacy consumer's refusal stays word for word: its status-list ids carry no tokens. Admission (:518) still runs before this gate, so the strict refusal is unreachable until verified-local is certified.

(b) tools/reportBlocked.ts. Pass the reporting row `task` as the consumer at:
- :234 satisfiedBlockedOnIds (isDependencySatisfied(state, id, task));
- :494 heldOnEvidence;
- :501 describeUnmetDependency(state, id, task).

(c) tools/setTaskDependencies.ts. Pass the caller as the actor: `state.updateTask(task.id, { dependsOn }, 'TASK_DEPENDENCIES_SET', params.workerId || undefined)`. The activity entry then names who changed the gate (activityLog: workerId = actorWorkerId). Keep the role gate, the system message (it already lists +added/-removed for edits and 'was [...]' for a replace) and the response text unchanged; dependsOnUnmet is consumer-aware through unmetDependsOn. Removal writes only dependsOn: never a review, receipt, check or status.

All other unmetDependsOn sites become consumer-aware with no edit: getContext, listTasks, searchTasks, claimEligibility, resourceStore, setTaskDependencies. V12b (task-6339299a) proves projection agreement over MCP. Do not touch claimGuards.ts, delete_task or any doc: V12 owns the docs sweep.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, last (load adversarial-self-review).

MUTANTS: on scratch copies in the snapshot, one exact replacement each, then restore and cmp. Kill only by real test failures: a no-tests or compile failure is a false kill.
- M1 drop the verified-local-snapshot check: the DoD1 legacy-captured row.
- M2 a strict consumer treats a missing id as satisfied: the DoD1 missing and delete_task rows.
- M3 ARCHIVED satisfied without a receipt: the DoD2 receipt row.
- M4 accept an approval on any candidate: the older-candidate row.
- M5 `.some(approve)` instead of the LAST review: the later-reject row.
- M6 unmetDependsOn ignores its consumer: the unblock/claim path rows.
- M7 reportBlocked without the consumer: its row.
- M8 setTaskDependencies without the actor: the DoD3 audit row.
- M9, the rejected design: strictness from `resolveTaskDeliveryPolicy(...) !== 'legacy'`. It must break existing rows, which proves the M01f boundary. At the architect's prototype that was 14 rows incl. executionPolicyIntegration E1-control and dependencyUnblock.test.ts's strict-policy rows.

Then read the diff as an attacker trying to release a strict consumer early:
- a path still judging without the consumer;
- a forged or late review or receipt (both stores are append-only; only the LAST review on the CURRENT candidate and that candidate's single receipt count);
- a status flip, delete or removal manufacturing proof;
- a malformed snapshot or setting reading as legacy (it must fail closed);
- legacy byte-identity of every message;
- cost: for strict consumers only, each prerequisite does linear store scans; legacy consumers pay one profile read;
- no .moe edits, no forbidden tokens, no new activity types (ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES is mirrored in moe-vscode).
Keep the non-board diff at or under 400 net lines.

If a finding changes a file, rerun the step-5 gate fresh and submit that output. Write the handoff memory.

CHOSEN: strictness is the PROFILE dimension, exactly as M01c/e/f use 'strict' ('A strict task throws EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY').
- Consumer: resolveTaskExecutionProfile(settings, consumer.snapshot) === 'verified-local'.

- docs (V12's sweep).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A verified-local (strict) consumer counts a prerequisite as satisfied only on retained verified delivery: the prerequisite's OWN captured snapshot is verified-local, evaluateDeliveryEvidence is satisfied, the last review on its current candidate is an approval, and, when ARCHIVED, that candidate has a delivery receipt. A missing or deleted id, a legacy-captured DONE row, a status-flipped DONE and an ARCHIVED row without proof never count. Legacy and observe consumers keep today's answers under every live deliveryPolicy. Removing a dependency stays role-gated and is now attributed to its actor in the activity log, and it never writes evidence.
